Here are the outcomes, taken from the spec's rulings R1–R11 and phrased as what you get. They are **unranked**, so the order below is only the order of the spec.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for one real archived quarter, with rows parsed and normalized to the `sec-index-v1` contract | R1, R3, §4.4, §4.6 | One quarterly `master.idx`. Its size is unknown until it is listed or fetched (see the probe below). |
| O2 | The historical baseline over your chosen quarter range, with a per-quarter result report and every gap named | R1, R5, §4.2 Backfill, §4.6 Parse | 4 quarterly files per year of range. §4.8 sets no start year, so the total isn't known yet. Older index formats need golden fixtures, which costs your time to build. |
| O3 | Daily indexes added as they appear, with catch-up after missed runs, including across quarter boundaries | R2, R5, §4.2 Daily | Roughly 250 daily files a year, one per business day. Individual sizes are unverified. |
| O4 | Stored raw files reprocessed after a parser change, with no new SEC download | R6, §4.5 | Compute only. It can't be estimated without running the work. |
| O5 | Weekly reconciliation of quarterly corrections: additions and updates are recorded, and removals are held until you approve them against the source hash | R7, R10, §4.4 | §4.2 re-downloads every supported quarter each run, so each week moves about the baseline's full byte volume again. Approvals also take your time on an ongoing basis. |
| O6 | Readers see only complete quarter versions, reached through one active pointer | R9, §4.6 | Small. No separate data volume. |
| O7 | All SEC requests go through one shared, throttled downloader at 3 req/s, with retries counted against that budget | R8, R11, §4.3, §4.8 | Wall time only. At 3 req/s, even a few hundred files take minutes of request time, so bytes matter more than request count. |
| O8 | Unattended operation on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage and alerts | R4, R11, §4.1, §4.7, §4.9, §7 Phase 2 | Azure spend is unknown until deployed. §2.2 explicitly makes no cost guarantee. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: source manifest and provenance, fault-injection and recovery test suite, operator runbooks.

**Tracks.** I propose a single track:

- **A — SEC filing-index catalog (known progression).**
- I considered splitting off O5 (reconciliation) and O8 (Azure operation). Neither stands without the catalog that O1–O3 produce, so they depend on it rather than answering an unrelated question.
- I call the track a known progression because spec §7 already orders the work from code to scheduled operation. If you think the historical-format coverage or the platform choice is still open, the track should be research instead.

**Choices already made**
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`) in a uv workspace.
- Spec §4.9 puts all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The other three scaffolds (`sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest`) are not in the spec.
- Not yet made: the ADR and the spec are both still *Proposed*, so the Azure platform in R4/O8 is not yet an accepted choice.

The roadmap file will be `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`, named after the spec's stem.

**Optional probe.** One SEC request for a single quarter's `full-index/<year>/QTR<n>/index.json` listing would give real file sizes and firm up the cost notes for O1, O2 and O5. I'd run it only if you say yes, and I'd need the User-Agent identity (name and contact) you want it sent with.

**Your call:** please rank O1–O8, and confirm or change the single track and its kind. While you're at it, tell me whether the three extra package scaffolds stay out of scope and whether R4's Azure platform counts as decided.
